# Foreman SOP This is the list of procedures, responsibilities, and duties of the [color=#c8a404][bold]Foreman[/bold][/color] of this station.
The Foreman is a senior role to all other [color=#c8a404][bold]Engineering[/bold][/color] personnel except the [color=#1b67a5][bold]Chief Engineer[/bold][/color].
When selecting an Acting CE, the Foreman should be considered above all other Engineering staff. Should the CE become incapacitated, the Foreman should assume the role of acting head as soon as is convenient for the situation. The Foreman as an acting head will fully assume the associated responsibilities, including ensuring the efficacy of the department as a whole instead of solely focusing on training.
The Foreman shares all responsibilities of other Engineering staff but is to prioritize training, directing, and advising their staff, even during station-threatening events. To this end, the appropriate role's SOP should be consulted depending on whom the Foreman instructs. Mind that the [color=#1b67a5][bold]Chief Engineer[/bold][/color]'s orders are final on how the department will operate and what orders must be followed. Failure to perform these priorities or to act as a role model is grounds for demotion.
1. The Foreman is expected to instruct [color=#c8a404][bold]Technical Assistants[/bold][/color] on how to perform their duties and to guide other Engineering personnel should they ask for help. [bold]Technical Assistants are to be prioritized first[/bold], but should the assistant decline help, the Foreman does not need to focus their attention on them. The Foreman should be open-minded to all available methods when teaching staff, even if it may not be the most familiar to the Foreman.
2. The Foreman is expected to fulfill the duties of other Engineering personnel [bold]if and only if[/bold] there are no Technical Assistants needing to be instructed. In addition, when assuming other duties, the Foreman is expected to follow the same SOP as the role they will perform.
3. The Foreman is expected to have a comprehensive understanding of the SOP and duties of each departmental role and may be consulted at any time regarding proper procedure. Additionally, the Foreman must ensure their department is following SOP and is expected to remind staff and/or the department head to do so.
4. The Foreman should be clearly distinguishable from other staff of their department, meaning that they ought to wear the appropriately designated clothing for their role. Consequently, the Foreman should not give to other personnel any Nanotrasen property assigned to them except for instructional use or in case of station-threatening emergency.
5. The Foreman is permitted to acquire surplus equipment and apparel of their department explicitly for training purposes.
6. The Foreman may ask certain departmental personnel to vacate equipment for the sake of training. However, this request may be refused if there is an urgent need or if it would be unwise to vacate at that moment. Unreasonable refusal to vacate is grounds for disciplinary action should the department head find it necessary.
7. The Foreman is expected to conduct routine inspections of the station's power engine(s) and of [color=#c8a404][bold]Atmospherics[/bold][/color] in 30-minute intervals. The Foreman is encouraged to use this inspection as an instructional opportunity for all present Technical Assistants.
8. The Foreman is permitted (but not necessarily required) to inspect each department after the first inspection of the station's engines. If a structural or design issue is noticed and able to be remedied, then the Foreman may work with the respective department head and the Chief Engineer to do so; otherwise, a fax to Central Command is appropriate.
9. The Foreman is not permitted to take the axe out of its case unless there is an immediate and urgent threat to their life or urgent access to crisis locations is necessary. The axe must be returned to the case afterwards, and the case locked.
